title: What bandsmen and stars earned
summary: Stars made about $500 plus record dates, ordinary sidemen $125-150.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What would you consider the average band salary was in those days?
Not the stars, you know just the side men I think you call them. Well when you were making $650 as a top man for instance.

Well that was, we were doubling in a show 'Hello Daddy' with Lou Fields and we were playing at the hotel. That's what we made, that was our salary. Mine and Benny Goodman's and I believe Jack Teagarden's was the same. Because we were feature men. But that was a lot of money even in those days.

Gosh I don't think we were, as I recall I think we did a couple of recording dates in there for that also. But that was our average salary I would say was around $500 and then 50 bucks a date and we used to do two or three dates a week.
But the average musician in those days? Average.
Well I mean the men in your own band for instance.
Oh they were making probably around $300 - $350.
That's what I wanted to know.
You would call that more or less standard salary?
Yes, those guys in that band. But we were working. I would say a regular band of musicians around, they weren't making any more than

$125 or $150 at the most. Other musicians. But we were a top band and working you know, plenty of work. But to be a feature man, you see there weren't too many men in those days that could, that were good jazz men along with being able to read the parts, sit down and read music. And we were capable of that. So we'd go on a recording date and they'd have some music there and we'd just play the melody the first chorus and then improvise on our choruses voices.
